What comes up in Rouse Hill

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. Treat the rows as the usual shape of the job locally. A specific property can differ, and that is what a site visit settles.

Pool and rear yard removal on an estate block

The commonest Rouse Hill job as the earlier estates mature and the back yards get rebuilt.

How it is handled
Shell broken out and removed through the side gap or over the fence where that is the only route, then the void backfilled and compacted in layers.
What does it
Mini or midi excavator with a hammer, tippers at the kerb.

Earthworks on release land

Bringing raw land to the levels the civil design calls for, usually before anything is built.

How it is handled
Cut and fill balanced where the design allows it, with imported material placed and compacted in layers.
What does it
Large excavator, roller, truck and dogs.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Rouse Hill

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Established estates beside land still being released So the work ranges from a pool removal on a fifteen year old block to bulk earthworks on raw land.
  • Newer stock with no asbestos assumption Post 1990 construction changes the survey, though it is still confirmed rather than assumed.
  • Tighter estate lots Where the side gap decides the machine on anything behind the house.
  • Clay rich soils Heavier and wetter than sand, and slow to dry out.

Rouse Hill estate streets are new and will take a tipper, but the lots are tighter than the older Hills holdings and the side gap tends to decide what can reach the rear. On the release land there is room for anything.

Rouse Hill questions

What people ask before we start

The house is from the 2000s. Do we still need an asbestos survey?
Post 1990 construction is far less likely to contain bonded asbestos, but the only way to know is to look. Where the build date is documented and the construction is consistent with it, the survey is a short job rather than a long one.
Can you get a machine into the back yard?
It depends on the side gap and what is in it. Where a gap will not take a machine, the work goes to a mini excavator or to hand removal with material carried out, and that is settled at the site visit.
There are large trees on the block. How does that work?
Tree removal depends on approval rather than on plant, and in this area it is routinely the longest item on a clearing programme. Retained trees need their root zones kept clear of plant and stockpiles, which frequently decides where the machine goes.
Does the asbestos work sit under your demolition licence?
No. Demolition licence AD214737 covers the structure. Removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists and clearance by an independent licensed assessor, because the assessor has to be independent of whoever did the removal. All of it is scheduled as a single job.
